6.2.rationale: The Indonesian Pasal 10(2) explicitly provides services for “perempuan dan anak yang menjadi korban kekerasan dan perdagangan orang” (women and children victims of violence and trafficking), listing complaint/identification, legal aid, health and psychosocial rehabilitation, social reintegration, repatriation, etc. This is clearly present in the retrieved English passage ([6.2-12]). If the indicator is about an “intersectional approach” specifically recognizing trafficking victims as a distinct group of women (often adult women) and tailoring measures accordingly, the text does not separate women trafficking victims from children; it treats “women and children” together and frames it as general victim services rather than an intersectionality-focused provision. The judge likely treated any mention of trafficking victims/services as satisfying the intersectional indicator, which is too broad. So the error is evaluation failure (indicator misapplied/too lenient), not missing evidence.
